title: How LLMs work (demo)

children.name: Tokens, IDs & vocabulary
children.summary:
- A tokenizer splits text into chunks from a fixed vocabulary, and each chunk has an integer ID ([explained](msg:2026-01-05.5))
- The ID is only a row number. Fed in raw, it would make neighbouring IDs look alike ([why](msg:2026-01-05.7))
- Diagnostic: you already knew text becomes numbered pieces ([your answer](msg:2026-01-05.3))

children.name: Logits & unembedding
children.summary:
- The last position's vector times W_U gives one logit per vocabulary token ([explained](msg:2026-01-05.7))
- A high logit means x points the same way as that token's column ([correction](msg:2026-01-05.10))

children.name: Softmax & temperature
children.summary:
- Softmax turns logits into probabilities; only differences between logits matter ([explained](msg:2026-01-05.10), [why](msg:2026-01-05.12))
- Temperature scales the gaps: T → 0 is greedy, large T is near-uniform ([your answer](msg:2026-01-05.13))
- Spaced review passed ([review](msg:2026-01-06.3))

children.name: Q/K/V & dot-product scores
children.summary:
- Each token makes a query, a key and a value; scores q·k/√d go through softmax to weight the values ([explained](msg:2026-01-06.5), [example](msg:2026-01-06.7))
- Separate W_Q and W_K because relevance isn't similarity ([correction](msg:2026-01-06.10))
misconceptions: Thought separate W_Q/W_K were for scaling (resolved)
Confused the value with the score (2026-01-08, re-test pending)

children.name: Loss & cross-entropy
children.summary:
- The loss is −log of the probability given to the correct next token ([explained](msg:2026-01-08.5))
- −log punishes confident mistakes much more than 1 − p ([your answer](msg:2026-01-08.6))

children.name: Gradient descent & learning rate
children.summary:
- Step every weight against its gradient, scaled by the learning rate ([explained](msg:2026-01-08.8))
- Too large overshoots or diverges, too small crawls ([your answer](msg:2026-01-08.9))
